mainTopic: Wart removal on שבת for the קרבן פסח, שמחת יום טוב, and רב אשי's challenge to רבי אליעזר
overview: The amud opens with a ברייתא where רבי שמעון praises doing a מצוה at its proper time: the fats are burned on שבת even though they could wait until night. Next, the גמרא sets our משנה, which says cutting a wart off the קרבן פסח does not override שבת, against a משנה in עירובין that allows cutting a wart in the מקדש. רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי בר חנינא resolve this in two ways. One splits moist versus dry, and the other splits by hand versus with a tool. Each side then explains why it rejects the other's answer. The גמרא then turns to the debate between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע in the משנה. רבי יהושע holds that שמחת יום טוב is a מצוה, and a ברייתא and the two פסוקים 'לה׳' and 'לכם' show the root of their disagreement. Everyone agrees that שבועות, שבת and פורים require eating and celebrating, and stories about מר בריה דרבינא, רב יוסף and רב ששת show the joy of these days and of תורה. Finally, רב אשי builds a קל וחומר from יום טוב to challenge רבי אליעזר's view that a שבות may be set aside on שבת for a מצוה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון praises doing a מצוה at its proper time
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה's line that burning the fats overrides שבת, the גמרא brings a ברייתא. In it, רבי שמעון points out that we burn them right away on שבת, even though burning is valid all night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said burning the fats overrides שבת. A ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון said: Come and see how precious a מצוה is when done at its proper time. Burning fats, limbs and inner fats is valid all night long, yet we do not wait until dark (after שבת). We burn them right away, even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה about burning the fats on שבת. It then brings a ברייתא where רבי שמעון draws a lesson from that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fats could have been burned on Saturday night without breaking any שבת rule, because הקטר חלבים is valid all night. Even so, the תורה wants it done immediately on שבת itself. רבי שמעון learns from this that doing a מצוה at its proper moment is very precious.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning the fats of a קרבן on the מזבח
It was taught in a ברייתא
A מצוה done at its proper time is precious
Limbs of the קרבן that go on the מזבח
Inner fats covering the organs

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the idea of חביבה מצוה בשעתה: doing a מצוה at its exact time has special value, even when a later time would also be valid.

phrases.english: "And burning its fats, etc."
phrases.notes: A quote from our משנה (burning the fats overrides שבת)

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon said:
Come and see how precious
is a מצוה in its proper time,
for burning fats, limbs, and inner fats
is valid all night,
and yet we do not wait with them until it gets dark.
phrases.notes: That is, until שבת is over

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: בֹּא וּרְאֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage by commenting on a line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burning the fats is done on שבת itself and is not pushed off to the night, which shows how precious a מצוה is at its proper time.

steps.title: Contradiction about cutting a wart in the Temple
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה says cutting a wart off the קרבן פסח does not override שבת. A משנה in עירובין says a wart may be cut in the מקדש, and is forbidden only with a tool.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said carrying the קרבן פסח, bringing it from outside the תחום, and cutting off its wart do not override שבת. But a different משנה teaches: One may cut off a wart in the מקדש, but not outside it. If it is done with a tool, it is forbidden in both places.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה and points out that a משנה in עירובין seems to say the opposite about cutting a wart in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lists חתיכת יבלת among the things that do not override שבת. The משנה in עירובין says that in the מקדש a wart may be cut, as long as it is not done with a tool. The two sources clash, and the גמרא needs a way to reconcile them.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying it (the animal) on one's shoulder
And they contrasted it with: a formula that opens a contradiction
A wart, which makes an animal blemished
The country, meaning outside the מקדש
A tool or instrument

steps.confusionAlert: The words "וכו׳" hide the key part of our משנה. Our משנה goes on to say that cutting the wart does NOT override שבת. That hidden line is what clashes with עירובין.

phrases.english: "Carrying it and bringing it, etc."
phrases.notes: Our משנה continues: and cutting its wart do not override שבת

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
One may cut off a wart in the Temple,
but not in the country (outside the Temple).
And if it is with an instrument —
both here and there it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line in the משנה and raises a contradiction against it
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that cutting the קרבן פסח's wart does not override שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in עירובין allows cutting a wart in the מקדש on שבת, so why does our משנה forbid it?

steps.title: First answer: moist wart versus dry wart
steps.stepSummary: One אמורא says both משניות speak of cutting by hand. Our משנה forbids it for a moist wart, and עירובין permits it for a dry wart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי בר חנינא disagree. One of them said: Both משניות are about cutting by hand. This one (ours, which forbids) is about a moist wart. That one (עירובין, which permits) is about a dry wart.
steps.whatsHappening: The first of two אמוראים resolves the contradiction by saying the two משניות describe different kinds of warts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A moist wart is still part of the animal's living flesh, so cutting it is forbidden even by hand. Since it could have been removed before שבת, it is not allowed even in the מקדש. A dry wart is basically dead and loose, so removing it in the מקדש is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one: both sources
Moist, still attached and alive
Dry, withered
By hand

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina disagree:
One said: both this and that are by hand;
this is a moist wart, that is a dry wart.
phrases.notes: Ours (forbidden) is moist; עירובין (permitted) is dry

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 2
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seem to describe the same act on the same kind of wart
steps.terutzMaskana: Same method (by hand), but a moist wart is forbidden and a dry wart is permitted in the מקדש

steps.title: Second answer: by hand versus with a tool
steps.stepSummary: The other אמורא says both משניות speak of a moist wart. עירובין permits cutting by hand, and our משנה forbids cutting with a tool.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one said: Both are about a moist wart, and there is no contradiction. This one (עירובין, which permits) is about cutting by hand. That one (ours, which forbids) is about cutting with a tool.
steps.whatsHappening: The second אמורא gives a different way to resolve the contradiction, based on how the wart is removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing a wart by hand is only a rabbinic prohibition, and that kind of גזירה does not apply in the מקדש. Cutting with a tool is a real מלאכה דאורייתא, so it is forbidden everywhere. Our משנה must therefore be talking about a tool.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is not difficult: there is no contradiction
One (of the two אמוראים)

phrases.english: And the other said: both this and that are a moist wart,
and it is not difficult:
this is by hand, that is with an instrument.
phrases.notes: עירובין (permitted) is by hand; ours (forbidden) is with a tool

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A competing answer to the same contradiction
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (by hand vs. with a tool)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seem to describe the same act
steps.terutzMaskana: Both concern a moist wart. By hand is permitted in the מקדש, and with a tool is forbidden.

steps.title: Why didn't the second אמורא use the moist-dry answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the אמורא who split by hand versus tool did not simply accept the first answer, moist versus dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who said "this is by hand, that is with a tool," what is the reason he did not say: both are by hand, and there is no contradiction, because this is moist and that is dry?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what is wrong with the first answer in the eyes of the second אמורא. This sets up the next step, which gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers seem workable, so the גמרא wants to know what pushed the second אמורא away from the moist-dry split. The question is a request for his reasoning, not an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to the one who says
What is the reason

phrases.english: And according to the one who says:
this is by hand, that is with an instrument —
what is the reason he did not say:
both this and that are by hand,
and it is not difficult:
this is moist, that is dry?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר: הָא בַּיָּד, הָא בִּכְלִי — מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers and asks why the second אמורא rejected the first
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the second אמורא would not accept the moist-dry distinction

steps.title: A dry wart crumbles off by itself
steps.stepSummary: The second אמורא would answer that a dry wart simply crumbles away, so a משנה would not bother to permit removing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would say to you: A dry wart crumbles off by itself. (So there is nothing to teach about permitting it, and both משניות must be about a moist wart.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second אמורא's reason for rejecting the first answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing a dry wart is hardly an act at all, because it falls apart on its own. A משנה would not need to teach that this is allowed. So the משנה in עירובין must be about a moist wart, and the real difference has to be by hand versus with a tool.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you
It crumbles completely by itself

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers resolve the wart contradiction. (1) Moist is forbidden and dry is permitted, both by hand. (2) Both are moist: by hand is permitted in the מקדש, and with a tool is forbidden. The second view rejects the first because a dry wart crumbles by itself and needs no teaching.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
A dry wart crumbles away by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A dry wart falls apart on its own, so a משנה permitting its removal would teach nothing. Therefore both משניות must concern a moist wart.

steps.title: Why didn't the moist-versus-dry answer use hand-versus-tool?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the question from Step 5. It asks why the first אמורא, who said 'moist versus dry,' did not say 'both are moist: by hand versus with a tool.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says both משניות speak of cutting by hand, and there is no contradiction because one is about a moist wart and the other about a dry wart: why didn't he say that both speak of a moist wart, and there is no contradiction because one is by hand and the other is with a tool?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same question in reverse. In Step 5 it asked why the second אמורא rejected 'moist versus dry.' Now it asks why the first אמורא rejected 'hand versus tool.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each אמורא picked a different way to split the two משניות. The second אמורא already explained why he rejected 'moist versus dry' in Step 6. Now the first אמורא must explain what is wrong with 'hand versus tool.'

keyTerms.meaning: And according to the one who says
This one and that one (both sources)
What is the reason he did not say?
Moist / dry (describing the wart)

phrases.english: And according to the one who says: both this and that are by hand,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּלַחָה, הָא בִּיבֵשָׁה —
phrases.english: and it is not difficult: this is a moist one, that is a dry one —
phrases.notes: This is the first אמורא's answer from Step 3.

phrases.english: what is the reason he did not say:
both this and that are a moist one,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בַּיָּד, הָא בִּכְלִי?
phrases.english: and it is not difficult: this is by hand, that is with a tool?
phrases.notes: This is the second אמורא's answer from Step 4.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of the question in Step 5, now aimed at the other אמורא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the first אמורא rejected the hand-versus-tool distinction

steps.title: The tool case is already stated in עירובין
steps.stepSummary: The first אמורא answers that the משנה in עירובין already says that cutting with a tool is forbidden everywhere. So our משנה would not need to teach it again.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: the case of a tool is already taught there: 'If with a tool, it is forbidden both here and there.'
steps.whatsHappening: The first אמורא explains his choice. If our משנה were only about cutting with a tool, it would be repeating something the משנה in עירובין already says outright.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עירובין משנה itself states that cutting with a tool is forbidden 'here and there,' meaning both in the מקדש and outside it. Reading our משנה as being about a tool would make it a pointless repeat. So the first אמורא prefers moist versus dry, which gives our משנה a new point to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you (the defender's reply)
But it is already taught there
Here and there it is forbidden (in the מקדש and outside it)
A tool or instrument

phrases.english: He would say to you: a tool —
is already taught there:
'If with a tool, here and there it is forbidden.'
phrases.notes: Quoted from the משנה in עירובין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ כְּלִי הָא קָתָנֵי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The tool prohibition is explicit in עירובין, so our משנה would be redundant if it were about a tool

steps.title: How does the other אמורא handle the repetition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the second אמורא, who says our משנה is about a tool, deals with the fact that this case is already taught in עירובין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא asks the second אמורא to answer the point just made in Step 8, and the next step gives his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point from Step 8 is a challenge against the second אמורא's reading. The question is: why would our משנה repeat a law that עירובין already teaches?

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one? (How does the other opinion respond?)

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: Asks how the second אמורא (hand versus tool) responds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of Step 8 into a challenge against the second אמורא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the second אמורא thinks our משנה repeats the tool case

steps.title: Our משנה mentions a tool to show the מחלוקת
steps.stepSummary: The second אמורא answers that our משנה brings up the tool case in order to teach the מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The fact that it teaches a tool here comes to teach us the מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The second אמורא explains that our משנה is not a pointless repeat. It mentions the tool case because רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about it here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עירובין משנה gives the tool ruling without naming anyone. Our משנה adds new information: רבי אליעזר holds that even cutting with a tool is permitted for the קרבן פסח, while the ruling that it does not override שבת matches רבי יהושע. So the repetition is needed to show that there is a dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute or disagreement
It comes to teach us
Here (in our משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: Each אמורא rejects the other's answer for a reason. The first אמורא says 'tool' is already taught in עירובין. The second אמורא says 'dry' is not worth teaching, but 'tool' is worth repeating here to show the מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: That which it teaches a tool here,
the dispute of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע
it comes to teach us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The repetition is needed to show that the tool case is subject to the מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע

steps.title: רבי יהושע's argument fits his general view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the words of the משנה and notes that רבי יהושע argues from יום טוב because he holds that rejoicing on יום טוב is itself a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'רבי אליעזר said: If שחיטה...' and so on. רבי יהושע follows his own reasoning, since he said that rejoicing on יום טוב is also a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, the debate between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. It explains why רבי יהושע felt he could bring a proof from יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר rejected the proof from יום טוב by saying that preparing food on יום טוב is only optional, while the פסח is a מצוה. The גמרא explains that רבי יהושע disagrees with that premise, because he holds that שמחת יום טוב is also a מצוה. So in his view, the comparison between יום טוב and פסח stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering an animal
Following his own reasoning (consistent with his view elsewhere)
Rejoicing on the festival
Is also a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that the פסח is a מצוה. The question is whether eating on יום טוב is only optional (רבי אליעזר) or also a מצוה (רבי יהושע). That is why רבי יהושע sees יום טוב as a fair comparison.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וּמָה אִם שְׁחִיטָה וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: 'רבי אליעזר said: And if שחיטה...' etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, marking the next topic.

phrases.english: רבי יהושע follows his own reasoning
for he said that rejoicing on יום טוב
is also a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the debate between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע holds that שמחת יום טוב is a מצוה, which is why he compares יום טוב to the פסח

steps.title: ברייתא proving רבי יהושע's view of יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי אליעזר lets a person spend יום טוב either eating or learning, while רבי יהושע requires dividing the day, half for eating and half for learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says, a person on יום טוב has only this choice: either eat and drink, or sit and learn. רבי יהושע says: divide it, half for eating and drinking and half for the בית המדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove what it just said in Step 11, that רבי יהושע holds that eating on יום טוב is a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, a person may spend all of יום טוב learning, so eating is optional. For רבי יהושע, a person must give half the day to eating and drinking, so eating is required. This confirms that the two תנאים are consistent with their positions in our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
Sits and learns
Divide it (the day)
The study hall

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר treats eating on יום טוב as optional, so it cannot be compared to the פסח. רבי יהושע treats it as a מצוה (half the day), so for him יום טוב is a valid comparison.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is a key source for the obligation of שמחת יום טוב through eating and drinking, alongside learning.

phrases.english: As it was taught: רבי אליעזר says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ לְאָדָם בְּיוֹם טוֹב אֶלָּא,
phrases.english: A person has on יום טוב only this:
either he eats and drinks,
or he sits and learns.
רבי יהושע says: Divide it,
half of it for eating and drinking,
and half of it for the study hall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim made in Step 11
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהושע holds שמחת יום טוב is a מצוה, while רבי אליעזר treats it as optional
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about how to divide the day of יום טוב

steps.title: Both opinions come from the same pair of verses
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע both read the same two פסוקים, one saying the day is 'for ה׳' and one saying it is 'for you.' They disagree only about how to combine them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Both of them learned from the same verses. One verse says, 'An assembly for ה׳ your God,' and another verse says, 'An assembly shall be for you.' רבי אליעזר holds: the day is either all for ה׳ or all for you. רבי יהושע holds: split it, half for ה׳ and half for you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן shows the source in the תורה behind the argument from the ברייתא in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק makes the day sound holy, for ה׳ (learning and davening). Another makes it sound like a celebration, for you (eating and drinking). רבי אליעזר says you may choose one of the two, while רבי יהושע says you must do both by splitting the day.

keyTerms.meaning: They both learned from the same verse(s)
An assembly / holiday gathering; a name for a יום טוב
For ה׳: spending the day in learning and davening
For you: spending the day eating, drinking, and enjoying
Split it (divide the day)

steps.whyThisMatters: Both sides now have a source in the פסוקים. The argument is only about how to fit two verses together, not about whether celebrating matters.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
And both of them expounded the same verse,
phrases.notes: Meaning they both dealt with the same textual question.

phrases.english: One verse says:
"An assembly for the Lord your God"
And another verse says:
"An assembly shall be for you."
Rabbi Eliezer holds:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ לַה׳, אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ לָכֶם.
phrases.english: Either all of it for God, or all of it for you.
And Rabbi Yehoshua holds: Split it,
half of it for God and half of it for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source behind the argument in the ברייתא of step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר reads the two verses as a choice (all for ה׳ or all for you). רבי יהושע reads them as a requirement to split the day.

steps.title: Everyone agrees שבועות needs celebrating too
steps.stepSummary: After a memory sign, רבי אלעזר says that even רבי אליעזר agrees that on שבועות we must also eat and celebrate, because it is the day the תורה was given.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory sign: ע-ב-ם.) רבי אלעזר said: Everyone agrees that on עצרת (שבועות) we also need 'for you.' Why? It is the day the תורה was given.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a short list of days where the argument does not apply, and everyone agrees eating and celebrating are required. The first is שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר normally lets a person spend יום טוב entirely in learning. On שבועות, though, we celebrate receiving the תורה, so the 'for you' part (eating and rejoicing) is required even according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign to help remember the order of the statements
Everyone agrees
That we also need 'for you' (eating and celebrating)
What is the reason?
The day on which the תורה was given

steps.confusionAlert: Here עצרת means שבועות. In the פסוקים of the previous step, the word עצרת referred to other יום טוב days (שביעי של פסח and שמיני עצרת). Do not mix them up.

phrases.english: (Ayin-Beit-Mem is a mnemonic)
phrases.notes: ע from עצרת, ב from שבת, ם from פורים: the order of the next three statements.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
All agree regarding Atzeret (Shavuot)
that we also require "for you."
What is the reason?
It is the day on which the Torah was given.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בַּעֲצֶרֶת דְּבָעֵינַן נָמֵי לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the argument of step 13: on שבועות even רבי אליעזר requires celebrating.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבועות, everyone agrees there must also be eating and celebrating.

steps.title: Everyone agrees שבת needs enjoyment too
steps.stepSummary: רבה says everyone agrees that שבת also needs 'for you,' because the פסוק calls שבת a delight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Everyone agrees that on שבת we also need 'for you.' Why? Because it says, 'And you shall call שבת a delight.'
steps.whatsHappening: The second item on the list: שבת also requires physical enjoyment, according to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ישעיה calls שבת עונג, a delight. That means pleasure, like good food, is part of שבת itself, so even רבי אליעזר would not allow a שבת spent only learning without enjoyment.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sabbath
Delight, pleasure
And you shall call

phrases.english: Rabba said:
All agree regarding Shabbat
that we also require "for you."
What is the reason?
"And you shall call Shabbat a delight."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּשַׁבָּת דְּבָעֵינַן נָמֵי לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second day, שבת, to the list started in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת everyone agrees there must also be enjoyment, based on 'וקראת לשבת עונג.'

steps.title: Everyone agrees פורים needs feasting too
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says everyone agrees that פורים needs 'for you,' because the מגילה calls it days of feasting and joy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Everyone agrees that on פורים we also need 'for you.' Why? Because 'days of feasting and joy' is written about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The third and last item on the list: פורים requires eating and celebrating, according to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מגילה itself defines פורים as days of משתה ושמחה, feasting and rejoicing. So celebrating is the main point of the day, and no one could say to spend it only in learning.

keyTerms.meaning: The holiday of Purim
Days of feasting and joy
It is written about it

steps.whatToRemember: Three days where everyone agrees eating and celebrating are required (memory sign עב״ם): שבועות, because the תורה was given; שבת, because it is called עונג; and פורים, because of משתה ושמחה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
All agree regarding Purim
that we also require "for you."
What is the reason?
"Days of feasting and gladness" is written about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּפוּרִים דְּבָעֵינַן נָמֵי לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of three days begun in steps 14 and 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On פורים everyone agrees there must be feasting and joy.

steps.title: מר בריה דרבינא fasted all year except three days
steps.stepSummary: A story: מר בריה דרבינא fasted every day of the year except שבועות, פורים, and ערב יום כיפור. He did not fast on שבועות because the תורה was given then, and not on פורים because of 'feasting and joy.'
steps.simpleTranslation: מר, the son of רבינא, would fast the whole year, except for שבועות, פורים, and ערב יום כיפור. שבועות, because it is the day the תורה was given. פורים, because 'days of feasting and joy' is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that matches the list it just gave. A very pious אמורא who fasted daily still stopped fasting on these special days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even someone who chose to fast every day knew that שבועות and פורים require eating, for the same reasons given in steps 14 and 16. The third exception, ערב יום כיפור, is new, and its reason is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The whole year
Sat in fasting: he would fast
Except for
The day before יום כיפור (ערב יום כיפור)

steps.confusionAlert: שבת is not on his list. He did not fast on שבת either, since fasting on שבת is generally not allowed, so it did not need to be mentioned as a special exception.

phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina,
would spend the whole year fasting,
except for Shavuot, and Purim,
and the eve of Yom Kippur.
Shavuot: it is the day on which the Torah was given.
Purim: "days of feasting and gladness" is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא כּוּלַּהּ שַׁתָּא הֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּתַעֲנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the rulings of steps 14 and 16 being practiced, and adds a new day (ערב יום כיפור).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a constant faster must eat on שבועות, פורים, and ערב יום כיפור.

steps.title: Why eating on ערב יום כיפור counts like fasting
steps.stepSummary: The reason for not fasting on ערב יום כיפור comes from a teaching of חייא בר רב מדפתי. The פסוק says to afflict yourselves on the ninth, though the fast is on the tenth. This teaches that eating on the ninth counts as if one fasted on both days.
steps.simpleTranslation: ערב יום כיפור: as חייא בר רב of Difti taught: 'And you shall afflict yourselves on the ninth of the month.' Do we fast on the ninth? We fast on the tenth! Rather, it is teaching you: whoever eats and drinks on the ninth, the פסוק counts it for him as if he fasted on the ninth and the tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to explain the third exception in the story, ערב יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to place the fast on the 9th, but יום כיפור is on the 10th. The answer is that the 9th is mentioned because eating on it is itself a מצוה, so valuable that it counts like a second day of fasting. That is why מר בריה דרבינא would not fast then.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught (a ברייתא-style teaching)
And you shall afflict yourselves (fast)
Is it really so? (a question showing surprise)
The פסוק counts it for him
The ninth and the tenth (of תשרי)

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'Do we fast on the ninth?' is not an attack on the הלכה. It is part of the teaching itself, a puzzle in the פסוק that leads to the lesson.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known מצוה to eat on ערב יום כיפור.

phrases.english: The eve of Yom Kippur:
as Chiyya bar Rav of Difti taught:
"And you shall afflict your souls
on the ninth of the month"
But do they fast on the ninth?
Don't they fast on the tenth!
Rather, it is to tell you:
Anyone who eats and drinks on the ninth,
the verse credits him
as if he fasted on the ninth and the tenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the reason for the third exception mentioned in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That one should not fast, and should eat, on ערב יום כיפור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of חייא בר רב מדפתי on ויקרא 23:32, 'ועניתם את נפשותיכם בתשעה לחודש.'

steps.title: רב יוסף's special שבועות feast
steps.stepSummary: On שבועות, רב יוסף asked for a choice calf to be prepared. He said that without this day, when the תורה was given, he would be just one of many ordinary Yosefs in the market.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף, on the day of שבועות, said: Prepare me a choice third-born calf. He said: If not for this day that caused it, how many Yosefs are there in the market!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story, showing how an אמורא celebrated שבועות with a special meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף explains that his greatness came only from the תורה given on this day. Without it he would be an ordinary person, one of many people named Yosef. So he felt a personal duty to celebrate שבועות in a big way, which matches רבי אלעזר's rule in step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: Prepare for me
A choice calf (third-born, or one third grown)
Caused
The marketplace

steps.whatToRemember: שבועות is a day everyone must celebrate with eating and joy, because it is the day the תורה was given. רב יוסף's feast shows how much the תורה shapes a person.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef, on the day of Shavuot, said:
Prepare for me a choice third-born calf.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר, אִי לָא הַאי יוֹמָא דְּקָא גָרֵים —
phrases.english: He said: If not for this day that caused it,
how many Yosefs are there in the market!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף בְּיוֹמָא דַעֲצַרְתָּא אָמַר: עָבְדִי לִי עִגְלָא תִּלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story illustrating the rule that שבועות requires celebration, closing the topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבועות should be celebrated with a festive meal, out of gratitude for the תורה.

steps.title: רב ששת rejoices over his monthly review
steps.stepSummary: Every thirty days רב ששת reviewed everything he had learned. Then he leaned on the door bolt and told his soul to rejoice, because he had learned for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every thirty days רב ששת would review his learning. He would lean against the bolt of the door and say: Rejoice, my soul, rejoice, my soul! For you I read מקרא, for you I learned משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells one more story about the joy of תורה. This one is about רב ששת, who celebrated after finishing each monthly review.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רב יוסף's story about שבועות, this shows a תלמיד חכם taking personal joy in his תורה. רב ששת says he learned 'for you,' meaning for his own soul. That wording sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Reviews his learning
The bolt or doorpost of the door
Rejoice, my soul
I read מקרא / I learned משנה

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet, every thirty days,
would review his learning,
and he would lean and stand at the bolt of the door,
and say: Rejoice, my soul, rejoice, my soul,
phrases.notes: He speaks directly to his own soul.

phrases.english: for you I read Scripture, for you I learned Mishnah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת כׇּל תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין מְהַדַּר לֵיהּ תַּלְמוּדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is another story about personal joy in תורה, following רב יוסף's שבועות story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may rejoice in his תורה learning as something done for his own soul.

steps.title: But the whole world exists because of תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת's words. רבי אלעזר says heaven and earth exist only because of תורה. So תורה is not just for one's own soul.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רבי אלעזר said: If not for תורה, heaven and earth would not continue to exist. As the פסוק says: 'If not for My covenant day and night, I would not have set up the laws of heaven and earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב ששת could say he learned 'for you, my soul.' According to רבי אלעזר, תורה keeps the entire world going.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's words make it sound as if תורה benefits only the learner. רבי אלעזר reads the פסוק in ירמיה to mean that the 'covenant day and night' is תלמוד תורה, and that it holds up all of creation. The two ideas seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (opens a challenge)
If not for
My covenant day and night (here: תורה learning)
The laws of heaven and earth

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
If not for the Torah,
heaven and earth would not endure,
as it is stated: 'If not for My covenant by day and by night,'
'I would not have set up the laws of heaven and earth!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording 'for you' in רב ששת's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that he learned 'for you, my soul'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If תורה keeps the whole world in existence, its benefit is universal. So it is not only for the learner's own soul.

steps.title: At first a person learns for himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both ideas are true. תורה does sustain the world, but when a person first learns, he does it with his own benefit in mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the beginning, when a person does it, he does it with himself in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. A person's first reason for learning is personal, even though the learning also benefits the whole world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not deny רבי אלעזר's teaching. It explains that רב ששת was describing the learner's own starting point: he learns for his own soul. The larger, world-sustaining effect comes along with it.

keyTerms.meaning: At the outset / at first
With himself in mind

steps.whatToRemember: תורה sustains the whole world, but a person starts learning for his own soul. That is why רב ששת could say 'for you, my soul.'

phrases.english: At the outset, when a person does it,
he does it with himself in mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge from רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reconciles the two statements by separating the learner's first intention from the wider effect of his learning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'For you, my soul' sounds as if תורה benefits only the individual.
steps.terutzMaskana: תורה benefits the whole world, but a person begins learning for his own sake.

steps.title: רב אשי's קל וחומר against רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that even if we accept רבי אליעזר's view that יום טוב is רשות, his position can be refuted. On יום טוב, optional מלאכה is allowed, yet a שבות is still forbidden. So on שבת, where only מלאכה for a מצוה is allowed, a שבות should surely stay forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even according to what רבי אליעזר said, that יום טוב is optional, there is a refutation. On יום טוב, the תורה allowed מלאכה even for an optional need, and still it did not allow the שבות that goes with it. On שבת, the תורה allowed only מלאכה for a מצוה. Isn't it logical that it should not allow the שבות that goes with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The stories are over, and the גמרא returns to the legal topic. רב אשי builds a קל וחומר that challenges רבי אליעזר's view that a rabbinic שבות may be set aside on שבת for a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think רבי אליעזר could brush off a proof from יום טוב, since he holds יום טוב joy is optional (רשות). רב אשי turns that very point into the argument. יום טוב is the more lenient day, since even optional מלאכה is allowed, yet the שבות stays forbidden. So שבת, the stricter day where only מלאכה for a מצוה is allowed, should certainly keep the שבות forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Rejoicing on יום טוב is optional (רבי אליעזר's view)
A refutation of a logical argument
A rabbinic prohibition on שבת or יום טוב
Forbidden labor done for an optional purpose
Is it not logical? (קל וחומר formula)

steps.confusionAlert: The two kinds of permission point opposite ways here. יום טוב allows MORE מלאכה, since even optional needs are allowed. That makes it the lenient case. The קל וחומר runs from lenient יום טוב to strict שבת, and its conclusion is that the שבות is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument goes back to the core מחלוקת of the משנה about whether a שבות may be set aside on שבת for the קרבן פסח. It shows that רבי אליעזר's reasoning faces a challenge even on his own terms.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
And even according to what Rabbi Eliezer said,
that rejoicing on Yom Tov is optional,
there is a refutation against him:
If on Yom Tov,
on which labor for an optional purpose is permitted,
the rabbinic prohibition that goes with it was not permitted,
then Shabbat, on which is permitted
only labor for a מצוה,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא תַּתִּיר שְׁבוּת שֶׁעִמָּהּ!
phrases.english: isn't it logical that it should not permit the rabbinic prohibition that goes with it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: וּלְמַאי דְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר נָמֵי יוֹם טוֹב רְשׁוּת, אִית לֵיהּ פִּירְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories about תורה joy and returns to the legal debate over רבי אליעזר's view of יום טוב and שבות.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's position that a שבות may be set aside on שבת for a מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from יום טוב: if optional מלאכה is allowed there and a שבות is still forbidden, then on שבת, where only מלאכה for a מצוה is allowed, a שבות should surely be forbidden.
